output_text:
{
  "score": 7,
  "flaws": [
    "The grey roof panels completely enclose the chute and obscure the marble for almost its entire journey; a polished desk toy should showcase the marble's movement using open rails, slats, or transparent materials.",
    "Severe z-fighting and geometry clipping are visible along the outer side walls where the grey roof planes intersect the dark green walls (especially noticeable in the close-up and low-angle views).",
    "The leftmost support tower hangs partially off the back edge of the desk (clearly visible in the top-down view) and its wooden base blocks are missing, leaving the vertical posts resting directly on the desk/air.",
    "The dark blue catcher box over the white cup is overly bulky, blocky, and visually hides the target cup, making the end of the run look like an industrial hopper rather than an elegant desk toy.",
    "The track design is a single monotonous straight ramp; it lacks visual and mechanical interest such as curves, switchbacks, or open transitions."
  ],
  "summary": "The mechanism is 100% reliable (16/16 trials) and the office desk props (lamp, mug, books, spare marbles) establish a nice theme, but the marble run itself looks like an enclosed industrial trough with z-fighting issues, overhanging supports, and a totally hidden marble path."
}
